newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's monetary base expands 2.4 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's monetary base expands 2.4 pct in October.

text.p: Brazil's monetary base as measured by daily averages grew 2.4 percent in October, giving an accumulated 12-month expansion of 8.6 percent, the Central Bank said.
The bank also said net public sector debt in September stood at 256.2 billion reais, or 33.8 percent of gross domestic product, versus 253.1 billion reais, or 33.6 percent of GDP, in August.
Net internal debt in September was 223.5 billion reais or 29.5 percent of GDP, while net external debt was 32.6 billion reais, or 4.3 percent of GDP, the bank said.
The public sector operational deficit for the January-September period represented 3.8 percent of GDP, the same as the January-August period, the bank said.
The federal government and the Central Bank posted an operational deficit of 1.5 percent of GDP; the states and municipalities, 2.1 percent of GDP; and state firms, 0.2 percent of GDP.
In primary terms, the public sector showed a surplus of 0.03 percent of GDP through September, compared with a primary deficit of 0.14 percent of GDP up to August, the bank said.
According to daily averages, the monetary base in October was 17.653 billion reais, compared with 17.243 billion reais in September, the bank said.

Brazil's public sector borrowing requirement, encompassing federal, state and municipal governments, the Central Bank and state companies up to September was 33.3 billion reais, or 5.97 percent of GDP, compared with a deficit of 6.17 percent of GDP for the January-August period.
